publicWording: Your partner changes the problem while you solve it.
evidenceRole: Related open-skill research supports the broader changing-environment idea; local class structure shows how partners practice.

publicWording: One school study reported changes in selected teacher-rated behavior scores after 12 weeks of BJJ.
evidenceRole: One direct BJJ study and one Taekwondo study provide bounded context; neither predicts an individual SSBJJ outcome.

publicWording: A small BJJ study found changes in some fitness scores after six weeks of training.
evidenceRole: A small direct BJJ study supports a narrow group-level statement, not superiority or a personal promise.
prohibited: BJJ is a better workout than Pilates

publicWording: One study of adult BJJ athletes found changes in some physical and response-time scores after live-task practice.
evidenceRole: The study offers narrow context for adult athletes; it did not test grappling skill, later recall, children, or beginners.

publicWording: A review of PE studies found mixed results for game-based teaching.
evidenceRole: Reviews of other sports and school PE provide context only; they do not test BJJ classes.
prohibited: SSBJJ method proven by these reviews

publicWording: A five-month study found group-level changes among people who chose BJJ or MMA.
evidenceRole: This observational study reports self-control, prosocial, and aggression scores; participant choice prevents causal claims.
